# CI, Branch Flow & Release Artifacts — Agent Guide

Doctrine for the workflows in this directory. The enclave-measurement chain these workflows verify is described in `crates/measure-enclave/AGENTS.md`; release/trust background in `docs/releases.md` and `docs/trust-root.md`.

## Branch flow (`next` → `main`)

`next` is the integration trunk; `main` is the verified, promotion-only branch. Feature/dependency PRs target `next` (Dependabot points at `next`). **The single human rule: never commit to `main` directly — everything funnels through `next`.**

- **Cheap workflows** (`rust-checks`, `cla`, `dependency-review`, `codeql`, `zizmor`, `pinact`) run on `next` PRs. `rust-checks` always *triggers* but path-scopes its work: a first `scope` step diffs the PR and independently selects the cargo gates, the Apple detacher/read-only archive regressions, and markdown lint. Rust source and crate inputs run the cargo gates plus Apple regressions; the Apple verifier/detacher/placer scripts, their tests, Mach-O parser, and fixture tree run the Apple regressions even on a script-only PR; markdown changes run rumdl. The archive regression preserves read-only directory modes in both inputs, requires the public verifier to reject duplicate or extraction-colliding members according to the actual temporary filesystem before extraction, rejects entries outside the exact top-level unsigned and detached layouts, and requires removal of its temporary extraction tree. Other docs/scripts/compose/Containerfile-only PRs skip these expensive steps. Editing `rust-checks.yml` itself forces every scope. The job always runs and reports (only the expensive *steps* are gated, so the required check never hangs pending); unrecognized files force the Rust gates; a full run is unconditional on every push and on **any** PR into `main` — so promotion always gets the real gate. The `next`/`main` pushes save the cargo cache that `next` PRs restore from.
- Scope classification lives in `.github/scripts/rust-check-scope.sh`; its adjacent executable test proves Apple-script selection and the combined Apple-plus-markdown fixture case on every workflow run.
- **The expensive `Build & Verify Artifacts` chain (`artifacts.yml`) does not run on `next` PRs** — it is scoped to `main` (push + the `next` → `main` promotion PR) and is the required gate for `main`.
- **Known blind spot in the cheap gates:** the Nix desktop packages compile from a per-package *filtered* workspace source (`flake.nix`'s `mkFilteredSrc`, which materializes only the crates that package needs), while `rust-checks` always builds the full workspace. A cross-crate manifest edge that a full-workspace `cargo` run resolves happily can therefore break release packaging outright and stay invisible until promotion — a `[dev-dependencies]` `path` edge between workspace crates is the instance we've hit. When you add or move a `path` dependency of any kind between crates, build `.#eidola-cli-macos-universal` (or the GUI equivalent for your platform) locally before promoting.
- **The merge gate for `main` is the `Guard` job in `artifacts.yml`:** on a PR into `main` it passes only for this repo's `next` → `main` promotion PR (and `push`/`v*` events), failing fast for any other head — short-circuiting the expensive chain (downstream jobs `needs: guard` and skip). Crucially it is **never green for an invalid head**: it's red on the `opened`/`synchronize` run, or never runs (check stays pending) if the base is flipped in via an `edited` event, which `artifacts.yml` doesn't listen to — so there is no success status an attacker could reuse by flipping the base back (the reuse concern from PR #151).
- `enforce-branching-strategy.yml`'s `retarget` job is convenience only: it moves any non-promotion PR's base onto `next` and returns success (failing only if it cannot retarget); the gate lives in `artifacts.yml`.
- **Promotion:** open a `next` → `main` PR (the collaborative surface where the full chain runs and integration/nondeterminism debugging happens); when approved and green, a maintainer comments `/promote` and `promote.yml` fast-forwards `main` to the validated `next` head SHA. The push is non-force, so GitHub rejects anything that isn't a fast-forward — `main` stays a strict ancestor of `next`, SHA-identical to a real `next` commit. `branch-guard.yml` continuously asserts `main ⊆ next` (push to either + every 6h) as a backstop.
- **GitHub config (not in-repo):** on `main`, require the `Build & Verify Artifacts` checks — `Guard` in particular **must** be required (the other jobs report *skipped* for invalid heads, which GitHub treats as satisfied; `Retarget onto next` is **not** required); restrict direct pushes to the promotion GitHub App as the sole ruleset bypass actor (its App ID + private key live only on the `main`-restricted `promote` Environment, so only `promote.yml` running from `main` can mint a token), and block force-pushes. On `next`: block force-pushes and deletions; `Build & Verify Artifacts` is not required there.

## Build & Verify Artifacts (`artifacts.yml`)

Four jobs:

- **`oci`** (ubuntu-24.04) mirrors the local `just update-manifest` flow end-to-end in five inline phases: (1) bake server + postgres, (2) stamp the fresh server digest into the workspace `tinfoil-config.yml`, (3) recompute the enclave from the stamped config and overwrite `releases/trust/server-enclave.json`, (4) bake cli (its build context COPYs the just-overwritten `server-enclave.json`), (5) emit the stamped config, recomputed enclave, and combined OCI partial as job outputs — and verifies the built OCI subset against the committed `artifact-manifest.json`.
- **`apple`** (self-hosted Mac: Nix-based macOS universal-binary builds — cli + GUI `.app`) and **`linux-gui`** (ubuntu-24.04: the Nix-built Linux GUI, a glibc dynamic binary — see `flake.nix`'s `eidola-gui-linux` for why it can't be static-musl StageX) both `needs: oci`, install the stamped config + recomputed enclave from `oci`'s outputs, and build their Nix desktop artifacts against that same trust root. The ordinary Ubuntu cargo-test gate runs the cross-platform Rust golden; the Apple job adds a deliberately narrow independent signapple check: exact arm64 slice + bundle seal equality on the settled fixture, while the classifier permits only signapple's measured x86_64 `__LINKEDIT` `vmsize` divergence.
- **`artifact-manifest`** gates on all three; it materializes `oci`'s outputs, runs `verify-full` (recomputes the enclave from the stamped config and compares the composed manifest to the committed `artifact-manifest.json`), and on PRs posts a REQUEST_CHANGES review whose body contains all three files (`tinfoil-config.yml`, `releases/trust/server-enclave.json`, `artifact-manifest.json`) verbatim. Because the workflow executes the entire generation chain inside one job rather than verifying disjoint partials, those three suggestions are guaranteed internally consistent: committing them as-is reproduces a fixed point of the chain.

**Apple signing custody.** The Developer ID private key is generated and retained on a distinct YubiKey PIV token; because CI is unattended, its touch policy is `never`. Its PIN is available only through the protected release-tag signing environment. Apple-signing’s non-deterministic assets and claims stay outside the deterministic `artifact-manifest.json`. Provisioning stops until the exact PIV slot, PIN policy, and noninteractive CryptoTokenKit unlock path are empirically proven on the actual runner; see the [Apple CI YubiKey runbook](../docs/contributing/release-apple-signing-yubikey.md).

**Build cache:** the `oci` job's StageX builds share a per-image registry layer cache (`ghcr.io/<owner>/eidola-buildcache:{server,cli,postgres}`, wired in `docker-bake.hcl` via the `CACHE_REGISTRY` bake variable inherited by the dev and `ci-*` variant of each image). The promotion PR builds the dev targets and the post-merge push to `main` builds the `ci-*` targets, sharing one ref per image so the push reuses the PR's fresh layers (registry cache rather than `type=gha` because the Actions cache ACL isolates a PR's cache from `main`'s run, and to keep the large cache out of the 10 GB Actions budget). `CACHE_REGISTRY` is **empty** for `v*` release tags (attested artifacts compile clean) and for any PR into `main` that isn't the promotion PR — only trusted producers ever read or write the shared cache; a stray or fork PR builds fully cold. `cache-to` carries `ignore-error` so a credential-less run degrades to a cold build. Cache poisoning is bounded regardless: every cached build's digest is verified against the committed manifest, and releases ignore the cache entirely.

## Pinned build tools

Not every tool the release path uses is a Rust crate in `crates/devtools/`. **`signapple`** (pure Python) is pinned as a `flake = false` flake input and packaged in `flake.nix` as `packages.signapple`; `flake.lock` is the pin. Its role is **the independent `apply`** our own reattach is differentially tested against — it is neither the signer nor the detacher. It cannot detach a signature it did not create, and its only detach path is a flag on `sign`, which demands a PKCS#12 archive that a non-exportable token key can never produce; detaching is therefore ours (measured, `scripts/fixtures/apple-roundtrip/round-trip.md` §1.1). It is **build-time and CI only** — it never enters `Cargo.lock`, never ships in an artifact, and never runs on a user's machine, which is why it may be Python and why `cargo-deny` does not see it. MIT, with two dependencies built from git revisions in `flake.nix` because nixpkgs cannot supply them — `certvalidator` (MIT, achow101's fork) and `elfesteem` (**LGPL-2.1**, which is fine precisely because nothing here is distributed); see the comment there. If a patch is ever needed, fork to `eidola-ai/signapple` branch `eidola` and follow the fork-branch rewrite practice in `crates/eidola-gui/AGENTS.md` (tag `pin-<shortsha>` before any force-push).

## Releases (`tinfoil-build.yml`)

Runs on `v*` tags, two responsibilities: (1) generate `tinfoil-deployment.json` from `artifact-manifest.json`, attest it to Sigstore via `actions/attest`, and create the GitHub release — the artifact Tinfoil's verifier chain consumes; (2) sign `artifact-manifest.json` with `cosign sign-blob` (Fulcio keyless via the workflow's OIDC identity) and upload the manifest + Sigstore bundle as release assets for the client's self-update verifier. **The filename `tinfoil-build.yml` is mandated by Tinfoil's closed-source deployment system — do not rename.** The release is intentionally not marked `latest` here; the release officer's tooling does that once their human attestation is signed and uploaded.

## Image tagging

`main` (rolling, updated per promotion), `v*` (immutable release tags), `sha-<short>` (per-commit). No `:latest`. Published to `ghcr.io/<owner>/eidola-{server,cli,postgres}`. The separate `ghcr.io/<owner>/eidola-buildcache` package (tags `server`/`cli`/`postgres`, each a single mutable ref overwritten in place) holds the BuildKit layer cache — not a release artifact.

## Other workflows

- `cla.yml` verifies every PR author/committer email is covered by the current `CLA-INDIVIDUAL.md` / `CLA-CORPORATE.md` hash recorded in `CLA-SIGNERS.txt`.
- **Dependency policy is checked from two angles with one shared license allow-list** (see the alignment note in `deny.toml`): `dependency-review.yml` reviews each PR's lockfile *diff* across all ecosystems (Rust crates, GitHub Actions — copyleft CI-only actions and first-party copyleft crates are exempted per-package via purls), while `rust-checks.yml` runs `cargo-deny check licenses bans sources` over the entire resolved graph (pinned via `crates/devtools`, so CI and `just check` run the same binary). `advisories.yml` runs `cargo-deny check advisories` on a daily schedule + dispatch instead of in the PR gate — advisories publish on their own clock, so a new one turns the scheduled run red rather than failing unrelated PRs.
- `website.yml` — PRs touching `www/**`, `docs/**`, or `crates/eidola-www` get a validating build (the content gate; `rust-checks`' scope step deliberately ignores `www/**`); pushes to `main` build + deploy to GitHub Pages.
- `rust-checks.yml` also runs `scripts/check-legal-doc-versions.sh` (a PR changing a legal document's bytes must increment its front-matter version by exactly 1). Currently short-circuited: the documents are pre-publication drafts, so the acceptance-ordering contract is not yet in force — the early exit in the script says when to remove it.
